A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same NAVER study and include readable main text, references and supplementary material. Inspection of the text, equations, tables and rendered figures supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original detection and segmentation evaluations, runtime measurements, component ablations, and self-correction and query-length analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a comparison of caption-based and direct visual entity-category extraction.

M1.justification: The five-state automaton, perception pipeline, probabilistic logic reasoning and answer verification remain unchanged. The caption-free alternative in new Table 12 is an ablation configuration, not a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate referring expression detection on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, RefCOCOg and Ref-Adv, and segmentation on RefCOCOg and RefCLEF. The additions use retained datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds GPT-4o-2024-05-13 and Qwen2.5-VL-72B as direct end-to-end grounding comparators. GPT-4o's earlier participation as an internal NAVER LLM is a different comparison. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: New Table 12 introduces an ablation configuration that removes captioning and replaces LLM-based entity-category extraction with direct VLM extraction. This adds an experimental control; the previously reported splits, metrics and full-system settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix Section 11 and Table 12 newly test captioning plus LLM category extraction against direct VLM extraction across four detection datasets. Existing component, model-selection, self-correction and query-length analyses are retained; the complexity analysis is relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds GPT-4o accuracies of 30.5/26.2 on RefCOCO/RefCOCO+ and Qwen2.5-VL accuracies of 94.6/92.2/90.3 on RefCOCO/RefCOCO+/RefCOCOg. Table 12 adds caption-free variant accuracies of 91.6/87.5/80.2/65.6 on RefCOCO/RefCOCO+/RefCOCOg/Ref-Adv. Previously reported scores and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal DFA definition, transition conditions and probabilistic logic formulation are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning explicit probabilistic reasoning, self-correction, interpretability, robustness and state-of-the-art grounding performance.

C2.justification: New Section 11 interprets larger ablation gaps on RefCOCOg and Ref-Adv as suggesting that textual scene summaries help reasoning about complex descriptions, and uses this to justify retaining captioning. Existing interpretations and the limitation concerning LLM code-generation capabilities remain.

D1.justification: NAVER's hardware and software disclosures, foundation-model settings, ProbLog-to-Scallop translation, six-retry limit and code-access information are retained. The five prompt templates are unchanged apart from numbering and placement.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Qwen2.5-VL Technical Report as reference 4 alongside its new comparison row. Other cited works and the substantive related-work positioning remain unchanged after matching renumbered references.

P1.justification: The complexity discussion moves from Section 4.3 to supplementary Section 7, and subsequent appendix sections are renumbered. Limited grammar and spelling corrections, an updated supplementary roadmap and an acknowledgments paragraph accompany the new ablation section.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains two rows, and v3 adds Table 12. The runtime table moves from main-text Table 6 to supplementary Table 10, with associated table and prompt reflow. Figures 1–4 retain their content and displays.

improvement.justification: The added direct-grounding comparisons in Table 2 and perception-pipeline ablation in Table 12 provide useful additional evidence for positioning and design choices while retaining prior results. The gain is limited: the ablation changes captioning and extractor type together, so it supports the combined pipeline choice without isolating the captioner's contribution.
